items.body: Pack 257 invites children aged 7 to 11 on a hike near Hidden Valley outside Riyadh on Friday 13 Nov, 8:00 am to 1:00 pm. Cost is 100 SAR per child, paid on the day, and a parent must stay for the whole event. Children need hiking shoes, a hat, a filled water bottle and a nut-free packed lunch, and those without shoes and a hat cannot take part. Register early through the online form, one per child.

All students aged 5 to 11 are invited, Scouts or not, with hands-on radio alphabet, Morse code and two-way radio activities. Families reserve a spot through the online page shared by the school. items.title: Scout radio event (Jamboree on the Air), Fri 16 Oct

items.body: Scout Pack 257 repeats its invitation to Jamboree on the Air at school on Friday 16 Oct, 1:00 to 3:00 pm. All students aged 5 to 12 are welcome, Scouts or not. items.body: Final reminder that Scout Pack 257's Jamboree on the Air is at school on Friday 16 Oct 2026, 1:00 to 3:00 pm. A preparation link was shared by the school to help children learn about communication before Friday and Saturday. It is also useful for children who cannot attend.

items.title: Buckswood shortlisted for MENA School Excellence Awards 2027

items.body: Tue 22 Sep was a normal school day. Parents invited 12:30 to 2:00 pm for refreshments and to meet homeroom and subject teachers. Dress code: green and white. No clubs that day. Buses ran as usual.
items.title: Saudi National Day celebration, 22 Sep

items.body: Strict nut-free rule: no peanuts, tree nuts, nut butters or spreads in lunchboxes, because some students and staff have severe allergies. From the Designated Safeguarding Lead and Head of Pastoral Care.
items.title: Nut-free school policy

items.body: Campuses closed on Ministry guidance. Teachers shared handouts in the morning, official online classes started the next day.
items.title: Online learning arrangements

items.body: Mute microphones when talking to family or when there is background noise. Send questions for the teacher through the Edunation messaging app after the lesson ends. Family members who appear on camera should be dressed appropriately, and students should not eat during lessons, only at break times. Keep Edunation push notifications switched on.
items.title: Online classes: reminders for parents

items.body: Following the latest Ministry of Education directives, online learning continues from Sunday 18 Oct to Thursday 22 Oct 2026. Students stay at home and all lessons are delivered online through Edunation and Zoom. Families should follow the updated online timetable already shared on Edunation.
items.title: Online learning extended, 18 to 22 Oct

items.body: The school shared a parent poster with tips to help children learn well during online classes. It covers getting ready before class, supporting your child during class, healthy routines after class and who to contact for help. Learners are asked to act respectfully, and a teacher may remove a learner who behaves inappropriately. For technical or attendance issues, message the homeroom or relevant teacher on Edunation.
items.title: Guide to online learning for parents

items.body: As online learning continues, families are asked to provide a bright, organised learning area with books and stationery ready before each lesson. Students keep cameras on throughout lessons unless the teacher says otherwise. Parents should keep the room quiet and not interrupt live lessons, and send any concerns through Edunation instead. Younger learners may need extra parental support.
items.title: Reminder: guidelines for a positive online learning environment

items.body: Families are asked to set up a bright, organised learning space with books and stationery ready before each lesson. Students should keep cameras on throughout lessons unless the teacher says otherwise. Parents should stay quiet and let teachers lead live sessions without interruption, and send any concerns or feedback through Edunation instead. Younger learners may need extra parental support to settle in.
items.title: Guidelines for a positive online learning environment

items.body: Following the latest government announcement, learning continues online on Tuesday 10 November 2026 through Edunation. Arrangements for the rest of the week will be shared once official guidance is received. Parents are asked to follow official announcements and school communications.
items.title: Online learning on Tuesday 10 Nov

items.body: Following Ministry of Education guidance, online learning continues from Sunday 1 Nov to Thursday 5 Nov 2026 through Edunation, on the regular timetable. Students should attend registration and all lessons on time, keep cameras on where possible and wear school uniform. Use a quiet learning space and keep family members off camera. Updates on returning to campus will follow when official information arrives.
items.title: Online learning continues, 1 to 5 Nov

items.body: Following Ministry of Education directives, the school moved to online learning on Sunday 11 October 2026. Students stay home and do not attend campus. All lessons are delivered remotely through Edunation. Further updates on school operations will be shared as needed.
items.title: Online learning, Sunday 11 Oct

items.body: The school shared its Online Learning Rules and etiquette document with parents. Families are asked to go through it with their child and help them understand the importance of being ready, respectful and responsible during online classes.
items.title: Online class rules and etiquette

items.body: To give students more time away from screens, each online lesson is now 35 minutes, with the usual 10-minute breaks between lessons. Two longer breaks were added: 10:05 to 10:30 and 11:50 to 12:10. The school day stays 8:00 am to 1:30 pm. The new timings are already updated on Edunation.
items.title: Online learning timetable updates for the coming week

items.body: Students should be ready before the first lesson, seated in a quiet place with a charged device and stable internet. Keep the camera on, stay seated and follow the teacher's instructions. The online timetable differs slightly from usual, with a 10-minute break between lessons. A short tutorial video on logging in to Edunation and joining classes was attached.
items.title: Online classes: reminders and tutorial video

items.body: Online learning will continue until further notice, in line with the latest Ministry of Education guidance. The school will share any change to the arrangements with all families promptly through Edunation.

items.title: On-site learning on Sun 1 Nov: awaiting official confirmation

Last week's spelling test and maths practice are already there under each child's name. Parents are asked to upload this week's spelling test too, even if it was already sent. items.body: The school is introducing an Authorised Pick-Up Card for families whose child is regularly collected by a driver, nanny or other authorised person. EduPik through Edunation continues as usual, and a pick-up request must still be created when the child is ready. The card shows the person's photo and details plus the names and classes of the children they may collect. To request one, complete the school's online form with a clear photo, one form per person, and tell the school in advance if the collector changes.
items.title: Authorised Pick-Up Card for drivers and nannies

Choose an experience linked to one of the 12 Pillars, take a photo of your child taking part and email it to the school's PR officer, saying which Pillar it shows and whether it may be featured on social media. Families are encouraged to consider the seasonal flu vaccine, teach good hand hygiene and covering coughs, and avoid sharing personal items. Children with flu-like symptoms should stay home until they recover, and families should seek medical advice if symptoms are severe or persistent.

Keep everything safe in a file or folder and do not discard any of it. The artwork will be displayed when learners return.

items.body: As part of the Who We Are unit, each student does an individual Spanish project and picks ONE option: a short video about themselves and their culture, or a poster with a short class presentation. Deadline is Thursday 15 Oct. A document with instructions, vocabulary and examples was attached; read it together with your child.

items.title: Print the Year 5 Spanish worksheet in case of online learning

items.body: To close the unit Where We Are in Place and Time, each student chooses a traditional dish from their own or another country and presents it in simple Spanish next week. The presentation covers the dish's name, origin, main ingredients and taste, and can be the dish itself, a photo, a poster or a short video. If learning stays online, presentations can be done virtually. Parents are asked to send photos as evidence of learning and use the attached vocabulary to practise.
items.title: Year 5 Spanish project: Sabores que viajan (Flavours That Travel)

items.body: The Spanish teacher shared two short videos and practice games on the verbs SER and ESTAR, both meaning to be. Children should watch the videos and memorise the present-tense conjugation of both verbs with all pronouns. SER is for identity, origin and characteristics; ESTAR is for location, feelings and temporary states.
items.title: Spanish revision: SER and ESTAR (Years 4 to 7)

items.body: Learners are asked to complete their chosen Street Art artwork and share a clear picture of the finished work with the Art teacher. The artwork should carry a clear message, idea or meaning, with creative colours, lettering, symbols and designs. A reference presentation was attached to guide the work.
items.title: Year 5 Art: finish and share Street Art artwork

items.body: As part of the 2D shapes unit, each child creates one display of triangles classified by sides (equilateral, isosceles, scalene) and by angles (acute, right-angled, obtuse), using clear labels and colours. Choose one format, such as a triangle museum, foldable booklet, triangle artwork, digital slides or a sorting game. Parents should supervise any cutting and let the child make and explain their own work.

Science: seedlings and how plants begin to grow. Drama: Martin Luther King Jr.'s speech and rights and responsibilities. A new student was named Student of the Week.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 2

items.body:
English, Drama and Unit of Inquiry: monologues and biographies, speaking and performance skills.
Maths: numbers in standard, word and expanded form, counting in powers of 10.
Science: pollination, seedlings and early plant growth.
Highlight: Saudi National Day celebration.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 3

items.body: Wrapping up the Who We Are unit: students studied five activists, presented freeze-frames and are writing and performing monologues. Maths: comparing numbers up to one million, negative numbers and a mental-arithmetic test. Science: seeds were planted and will be observed over the coming week. Highlight: the IB observation lesson went very well.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 4

items.body: Maths: Roman numerals and rounding numbers up to one million. Science: classroom plant observations finished and the plants went home to keep growing. The first Unit of Inquiry, Who We Are, closed with an assembly where students shared projects, freeze-frames and monologues. Photos and short videos of the assembly were attached to the email.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 5

items.body: English: the class began reading The Boy at the Back of the Class, linked to the new Unit of Inquiry, Where We Are in Place and Time (migration, belonging, friendship). Families are encouraged to get their child their own copy if possible. Science: the Earth's orbit and seasons. Maths: column addition, with column subtraction next week. Also covered: global trade in Global Citizenship, Britain's past and present in History, and friendship and inclusion in PSHE.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 6

items.body: The class teacher thanked students, parents and the school for another week of online learning and praised the children's progress over the past three weeks. This week students made their own bar graphs from the migration data the class collected and organised into a table. Parents are reminded to check the class Padlet and upload any work from this week. The teacher hopes for a return to offline learning soon.
items.title: Year 5, end of week 7 (online learning)

items.body: The class teacher thanked families for another week of support and for submitting tasks on time. It was an odd week, with two days in person and then back to online learning. Two students were named Students of the Week.

Unit of Inquiry: students complete a Global Citizenship and PSHE project on welcoming and supporting new students, and can post a video on the class Padlet or send it privately. English: personal narratives were finished in class, and anyone needing more time can complete them at home. Science: answer the written questions on page 168 of the Learner's Book in the science notebook and upload pages 167 and 168 to the class Padlet. Two Year 5 students were named Students of the Week.
